title: Africa 5 of 8 · Nile and Horn
edition: Africa countries · Eight regional lessons · John · November 2026
intro: Welcome to Africa episode five of eight. First, I clear the chosen names for a fresh regional lesson.

Six countries connect the Nile with the Horn: Sudan, South Sudan, Eritrea, Djibouti, Ethiopia and Somalia. Somaliland is demonstrated within Somalia’s stop, with its claimed independence explained separately.

states.name: Sudan
lines: Sudan lies below Egypt, east of Chad and north of South Sudan. Its northeastern coast reaches the Red Sea, while the Nile crosses its interior.
Gebel Barkal and nearby archaeological sites preserve temples, tombs and pyramids associated with the kingdom of Kush. Pyramids are part of Sudan’s history as well as Egypt’s.
Picture Kushite pyramids farther upstream from Egypt. Sudan is north of South Sudan and still has a Red Sea coast.
states.transition: Let's bring Sudan and its neighbours into view.

states.name: South Sudan
lines: South Sudan is landlocked below Sudan, west of Ethiopia and north of Uganda and Kenya. The White Nile passes through its interior.

The Sudd is an immense wetland associated with the White Nile, with channels, marshes and seasonally flooded grasslands. A great river can spread into a broad living landscape rather than remain one narrow line.
Picture the Nile spreading into marshes. South Sudan is the inland country below Sudan; it has no Red Sea coast.

states.name: Eritrea
lines: Eritrea follows the Red Sea coast east of Sudan and north of Ethiopia. Djibouti lies at its southeastern end.

Asmara, the highland capital, preserves a remarkable collection of early modernist buildings developed during Italian colonial rule. Cinemas, shops and public buildings form a distinctive urban landscape.
Picture modernist buildings above a long Red Sea coastline. Eritrea separates much of northern Ethiopia from the sea.
states.transition: Let's bring Eritrea and its neighbours into view.

states.name: Djibouti
lines: Djibouti is the small country at the meeting of the Red Sea approach and the Gulf of Aden. Eritrea is north, Ethiopia west, and Somalia’s northern region southeast.
Lake Assal occupies a depression below sea level and is famous for very salty water and salt deposits. The rift landscape reminds us that this region sits near separating tectonic plates.
Picture a salt lake beside the Horn’s narrow sea gateway. Djibouti is small and coastal; Ethiopia beside it is much larger and landlocked.

states.name: Ethiopia
lines: Ethiopia is the large inland highland country west of Somalia and south of Eritrea. Sudan and South Sudan lie west, while Kenya is south.
At Lalibela, medieval churches were cut directly into the rock. Some stand inside excavated trenches, so the surrounding stone was removed to reveal the building’s shape.
Picture churches carved downward into a highland landscape. Ethiopia is inland behind Eritrea and Djibouti; it does not have a coast.
states.transition: Let's bring Ethiopia and its neighbours into view.

states.name: Somalia
lines: Somalia forms the eastern Horn, with a long Indian Ocean coast and a northern shore on the Gulf of Aden. Ethiopia lies inland to its west and Kenya to its southwest.

In the northwestern Somaliland region, Laas Geel preserves prehistoric paintings of cattle and people in rock shelters. Picture those painted herds near the upper side of the Horn, above inland Ethiopia.

GeoClick also separates Somaliland in the northwest, which we show here as a related target. Its authorities claim independence; the simplified outline does not settle recognition, sovereignty or territorial control.
states.transition: Let's bring Somalia and its neighbours into view.

recap: Sudan lies below Egypt, with South Sudan below it. Eritrea follows the Red Sea, tiny Djibouti sits at the Gulf of Aden gateway, Ethiopia is inland, and Somalia forms the eastern Horn.

Recall Kushite pyramids, Nile wetlands, modernist Asmara, the salt lake, rock-cut churches and painted cattle near the Horn. GeoClick’s separate Somaliland target is a related selection, not another country counted in this series.
